decisions.evidence: R2 maker goal summary: 'organizes itself when you paste a link, avoids duplicates, and makes saved pages easy to rediscover through search, your own tags, and a focused read later list' — no display/navigation. R2 client: 'when I look at my list, I want it readable at a glance: the title, the little description, the tags, the site icon, all right there, and clicking one just takes me to the actual page.'
decisions.note: Early scoping. Client volunteers readable-list (REF-BM-07) and click-through-to-url (REF-BM-08), reference requirements absent from the maker's asked-about summary scope. Extend.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: paste link, 'the app gathers page details automatically.' R4 client: 'came back with the title... a short description... the site icon, the site name, and even a little preview image... I didn't have to type any of that myself.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Auto-metadata collection presented, conforms to REF-BM-02. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents only auto-gathered details. R4 client: 'One small thing... down the line — not now, just flagging it: I'd want to be able to fix that title or description myself if the app grabs something wrong or unhelpful.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Client requests manual edit of gathered title/description (REF-BM-03), missing from the auto-gather scope presented. Extend; delivered later at R27 (counted separately, different timing).

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: duplicate prototype, re-paste exact address. R7 client: 'it didn't make a second copy. Instead it told me "You already saved this link — here it is" and jumped me right to the existing one.' Client re-mentions edit-existing but says 'you already flagged it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Exact-duplicate → existing-bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06. The edit-existing remark is a re-expression of the R4 REF-BM-03/04 note, not a fresh capture (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'type Cooking, press Enter... tags are your own free-form words, added directly from the bookmark.' R9 client: 'the tag shows up right there on the bookmark. Adding my own free-form words directly on the item is exactly what I had in mind.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Basic assignment of a free-form tag conforms to REF-BM-09. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents single-tag entry, no suggestions. R9 client: 'a bookmark to be able to hold more than one tag... And when I'm typing a tag I've used before, I'd love it to suggest my existing tags so I don't accidentally make "cooking" and "Cooking" as two.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Autocomplete suggestions (REF-BM-10) absent from presented scope; multi-tag capacity (REF-BM-09 'or more') not yet demonstrated. Client requests both. Extend; delivered R12.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: type 'ita', choose suggested 'Italian'. R12 client: 'picking it left me with both tags on the bookmark and reused the spelling I already had. That covers both of my notes.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Multi-tag + existing-tag autocomplete delivered, conforms to REF-BM-09/10. Delivers the R9 extend.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: type 'Rome', then select Travel tag; 'word search covers the saved title, description, and web address... tag filters above the list.' R14 client: 'clicking the "Travel" tag narrowed it down to just the one travel bookmark... that combination is exactly how I'd want to find things.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Combined word-search over title/description/url plus one-click tag filter conforms to REF-BM-11 (and the title/desc/url portion of REF-BM-12). Approved.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'the search seemed to treat "Rome" and "rome" the same... Can you confirm that's on purpose?' Resolved R15 maker/client: 'You confirmed the "Rome"/"rome" matching is intentional, which is what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search conforms to REF-BM-13. Client sought and received confirmation of a conforming behaviour; resolved affirmatively (not a divergence).

decisions.evidence: R14 search covers title/description/url only. R14 client: 'if I've jotted my own note onto a bookmark, I'd expect that to be searchable too, the same as the description.' Kept alive R15/R18/R21.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 requires search over note as well; note-searchability absent from presented search scope. Client extends; delivered R23.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: flag Read later, open focused view; 'read-later items remain in the full collection while also appearing in their own view.' R17 client: 'landed on just that one bookmark — exactly the focused list... a read-later item still lives in my full collection while also showing up in its own view.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-later flag (REF-BM-17) and separate unread view (REF-BM-18) conform. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R17 presents flagging + focused view only. R17 client: 'once I've actually read one of these, I'd want a way to mark it as read so it drops off the read-later list. The setting it aside part is right; I just want the other half, clearing it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read (REF-BM-19) missing from the presented read-later scope. Extend; delivered R20.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker: 'Mark as read'; 'treated mark as read as clearing the read-later flag — not maintaining a separate reading-history record.' R20 client: 'it dropped out of the read-later list... still sitting there in my collection... marking something read just clears it off.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read clearing the flag conforms to REF-BM-19. Delivers the R17 extend; maker's no-history interpretation is orthogonal (no reference item).

decisions.evidence: R23 maker: add note 'Make this for Sunday dinner', search 'Sunday'. R23 client: 'searching "Sunday" turned up the pasta bookmark even though that word appears nowhere in the title or description, only in my own note... my personal notes should be findable the same way.'
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review. Note now searched alongside other details — delivers the R14c extend, conforming to REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker asserts 'each bookmark has one plain-text note.' R23 client: 'when I'm writing a note, I'd like to be able to give it a little formatting — say a couple of bullet points or a bit of bold — and have it show up nicely formatted... a touch richer than plain text. Can we plan for that?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-23 specifies a markdown note; the presented plain-text note diverges. Client supplies the reference-conforming richer/formatted behaviour in place of the mismatch. Correct; delivered R24.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker: make note a bulleted list, save, search. R24 client: 'it shows up on the bookmark as a proper readable list rather than one flat line. And searching "Sunday" still found the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Formatted (markdown-style) note rendered and still searchable — conforms to REF-BM-23, delivers R23 correction.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker: 'Edit title & description', change fields, save. R27 client: 'I changed the title... and the description to my own wording, saved, and the link itself, the site name, and the preview image all stayed put. Correcting the words the app gathered... is right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Title/description editing conforms to REF-BM-03/04. Accepted portion; the url-editing difference is split into the next decision (client corrects one, accepts this).

decisions.evidence: R27 maker: 'I've assumed only the title and description need manual correction.' R27 client: 'I want to push back a little... Sometimes... the address itself is slightly off... I'd want to be able to fix the address too, not have to delete the whole thing and lose my tags and notes... Can we add that?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Maker's assumption contradicts REF-BM-04 (edit url). Client rejects the assumption and supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (url editable, preserving other fields). Correct; delivered R28.

decisions.evidence: R28 maker: replace cluttered address with clean url, save. R28 client: 'Only the link updated... the title and description I'd corrected, my tags, my formatted note, the read-later flag, the site identity, and the preview all remained intact.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editable url preserving other fields conforms to REF-BM-04. Delivers the R27 correction.

decisions.evidence: R34 maker: unreadable page, 'saving the link with a clear details unavailable fallback... no invented description or preview.' R34 client: 'it still saved my link... a plain fallback title... No made-up description or fake preview, which I'd actually prefer.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Metadata-failure fallback is an edge-case elaboration of REF-BM-02 auto-collection; conforming. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R36 maker: paste utm-tracked variant; 'treated obvious tracking additions as irrelevant to page identity.' R36 client: 'it recognized it as the same page and took me back to the one I already had... those tracking tags don't change what the page actually is.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tracking-variant convergence conforms to REF-BM-06 duplicate rule; client endorses the same-page/different-page distinction. Equivalent refinement, not divergent.

decisions.evidence: R38 maker: enter 'recipes for Rome'; 'accepts complete http or https web addresses only.' R38 client: 'it kept my text right there in the box and told me plainly that it needs a full web address... The save box is for links, not a search bar.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. url-only save/validation conforms to REF-BM-01 (save by entering a url). Approved.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker: search 'volcanoes', '0 results with a clear no bookmarks match message.' R40 client: 'a clear "no bookmarks match"... my search word and the tag controls stayed put... an honest "nothing here" rather than the app quietly widening the search.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Honest empty-result state for rediscovery (REF-BM-12) conforms. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R42 maker: click × on Italian; 'removes the tag only from this bookmark — not from other bookmarks or your suggestions.' R42 client: 'took just that tag off this bookmark and left "Cooking"... it should only affect this bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Per-bookmark tag removal conforms to editing tags (REF-BM-04/09). Approved.

decisions.evidence: R44 maker: 'Show full note', search 'pecorino'; 'long notes should be shortened only in the collection view... all their words remain searchable even while collapsed.' R44 client: 'kept the long note tidied down to a short preview... searching "pecorino"... still found the bookmark, so nothing got cut off.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Long-note collapse preserving full formatted content (REF-BM-23) and searchability (REF-BM-12) conforms. Approved.

decisions.evidence: R46 maker: edit address to a genuinely different page, warn, 'Use details from the new page'; preserves tags/note/read-later. R46 client: 'it warned me that this looks like a different page... refreshed the title, description, site identity, and preview... but kept my tags, my formatted note, and the read-later flag intact.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Different-page edit with warn-and-refresh conforms to REF-BM-04 editing and REF-BM-02 re-collection; client endorses the ask-first behaviour. Not divergent.

decisions.evidence: R50 maker: Delete bookmark with confirmation; 'deletion removes that bookmark's note, tag links, and read-later state... tags still used elsewhere remain.' R50 client: 'it asked me to confirm before actually removing it... that bookmark was gone and everything else... stayed... a tag I still use on other bookmarks should stick around.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Confirmed permanent deletion conforms to REF-BM-05 (and the permanent side of REF-BM-27). Approved.

decisions.evidence: R50 presents only permanent delete. R50 client: 'I'd also want a gentler option — a way to tuck a bookmark out of my main list without destroying it... So I'd expect two different actions: this permanent delete, and a reversible "set it aside" that hides it but lets me get it back. Can we make sure that reversible option exists too?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reversible archive (REF-BM-26), its distinction from delete (REF-BM-27), and a separate archived view (REF-BM-28) are missing from the presented delete scope. Extend; delivered R52.

decisions.evidence: R52 maker: Set aside, open Set aside view, Restore; 'hidden from the main collection and its normal search, but remain accessible in their own view.' R52 client: 'made it vanish from my main list... showed up safely in the "Set aside" view, and restoring it brought it right back... clearly separate from deleting for good.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reversible set-aside hidden from list/search with its own view and restore conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28. Delivers the R50 extend.

decisions.evidence: R58 maker declares 22 behaviors settled, asks to implement. R58 client: 'Putting the list in an order I choose... I never got to say how they're sorted. I'd want to flip between newest first and oldest, or sort by title alphabetically.' Disposition R59: 'Sorting... recorded for a later cycle'; client 'holding you to them for next time.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sorting (REF-BM-22) missing from the settled scope. Client surfaces it and requests it; maker defers-but-records and client accepts deferral. Extend capture (surfacing does not require implementation this cycle). Single decision spanning R58 request → R59 disposition.

decisions.evidence: R58 client: 'Doing something to several bookmarks at once... I'd want to select a bunch of them (or everything currently matching my search or tag) and, say, tag them all or set them all aside in one go.' Disposition R59: 'bulk actions... recorded for a later cycle and were not quietly dropped.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) and apply-to-whole-matching-filter (REF-BM-21) missing from settled scope. Client surfaces both, maker defers. Extend.

decisions.evidence: R58 client: 'sometimes I'd want to search for an exact phrase in quotes, or say "this but not that" — combine words with something like "and," "or," "not".' Disposition R59: 'advanced quoted/boolean search... recorded for a later cycle.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Boolean AND/OR/NOT (REF-BM-15) and quoted exact-phrase (REF-BM-16) search missing from settled scope. Client surfaces, maker defers. Extend. (REF-BM-14 #tag syntax was never presented nor raised — a silent coverage gap, not a classifiable divergence decision.)
